A design philosophy viewed differently by stakeholders; for designers, it involves interface elements and layouts; for industrial designers, it refers to form (shape, size, look); for electronic engineers, it refers to hardware features like sensors, chips, and batteries; for application software developers, it involves following a development lifecycle to match user needs and expectations

Also referred to as user-centered design, human-centric design, or participatory design; an approach that involves users in the design process to understand their needs, expectations, and goals to increase usability.

USABILITY.name: USABILITY
descriptions: A measure of the goodness of a system from the point of view of the user; defined by ISO 9241-210-2009 as the extent to which a product can be used by specified users to achieve specified goals with effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction in a specified context of use
A measure of how good a system is from the point of view of the user, defined by effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction.
The broad category of metrics including effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction used to measure how usable a product is.
A measure of the ease of use of a system, which is enhanced by interaction design.
The goal of making a system usable with respect to a specific group of users, in a specified context of use, and for specific tasks.
The primary criterion used to determine which design is the "right" or "best" one among many possibilities.
A quality metric that determines if a system is usable from the end user's point of view, verified through empirical studies.
The quality of a system that makes it usable for the end user, which is a primary concern in interactive system development.
The main concern in interactive system development that must be taken care of to ensure a usable design.
The quality of a system or product when measured against a specified context of use or work context.
A measure of how well a system meets the needs and expectations of the users, which can be compromised if requirements are not gathered correctly.
A very important concern for XR systems, ensured by gathering end user requirements.
A measure of how easy a system is to use, which reduces if users cannot perceive their interactions or understand that something is happening.
The quality or aspect of the system that is being measured and analyzed through data collection and empirical study
A quality of a system that is evaluated through quick prototype evaluation and full-fledged robust usability testing at the end of system implementation.
The overall quality of an interface as measured by the data collected from users during tasks.

Also known as user-centric or human-centric design, focusing on the end user.
A design approach where the system is developed based on the user's abilities, context, goals, needs, and expectations.
A design approach where the importance of the contextual inquiry method was highlighted in 1988 (then called phenomenological research method).

BALANCE.description: A sense for which there is no specific organ; it helps in knowing head orientation and the direction of up.

TASTE.name: TASTE
descriptions: One of the six senses that relies on chemoreceptors to provide signals based on the chemical composition of matter on the tongue.
One of the direct perceptions involving sensory organs.
One of the primary human senses to be covered in the lecture.
A chemical sense involving the chemical reaction of chemoreceptors with stimuli arriving at the tongue.
One of the human senses discussed, noted as complex to generate effects for in virtual environments.
TASTE.description: One of the six senses that relies on chemoreceptors to provide signals based on the chemical composition of matter on the tongue. A chemical sense involving the chemical reaction of chemoreceptors with stimuli arriving at the tongue. One of the human senses discussed, noted as complex to generate effects for in virtual environments. One of the primary human senses to be covered in the lecture.

TOUCH.name: TOUCH
descriptions: One of the six senses involving motion, vibration, or gravitational force via mechanoreceptors, and temperature changes via thermoreceptors.
One of the direct perceptions involving sensory organs.
A sense of perception involving receptors in the skin to receive inputs from the real world.
TOUCH.description: One of the six senses involving motion, vibration, or gravitational force via mechanoreceptors, and temperature changes via thermoreceptors. A sense of perception involving receptors in the skin to receive inputs from the real world. One of the direct perceptions involving sensory organs.

SENSORY SYSTEM SELECTIVITY.name: SENSORY SYSTEM SELECTIVITY
descriptions: The phenomenon where bodily organs (receptors) are designed to be activated only when a specific type of stimulus arrives.
SENSORY SYSTEM SELECTIVITY.description: The phenomenon where bodily organs (receptors) are designed to be activated only when a specific type of stimulus arrives.

RECEPTOR.name: RECEPTOR
descriptions: A sensor within the sense organ that targets particular stimuli.
The initial structures that respond to a narrow range of stimuli across time, space, and frequency, sending signals to neurons.
RECEPTOR.description: The initial structures that respond to a narrow range of stimuli across time, space, and frequency, sending signals to neurons. A sensor within the sense organ that targets particular stimuli.

SENSORY ORGAN.name: SENSORY ORGAN
descriptions: The hardware of sensing in the human body which contains receptors.
SENSORY ORGAN.description: The hardware of sensing in the human body which contains receptors.

ELECTROMAGNETIC ENERGY.name: ELECTROMAGNETIC ENERGY
descriptions: Energy in the form of visible light that activates photoreceptors.
ELECTROMAGNETIC ENERGY.description: Energy in the form of visible light that activates photoreceptors.

VISIBLE LIGHT.name: VISIBLE LIGHT
descriptions: The frequency range of electromagnetic energy that photoreceptors target.
A spectrum of frequencies of electromagnetic light waves.
The range of light between red (700 nanometer wavelength) and violet (400 nanometer wavelength) that humans are able to perceive using photopic vision.
VISIBLE LIGHT.description: The range of light between red (700 nanometer wavelength) and violet (400 nanometer wavelength) that humans are able to perceive using photopic vision. The frequency range of electromagnetic energy that photoreceptors target. A spectrum of frequencies of electromagnetic light waves.

PHYSIOLOGY OF SENSES.name: PHYSIOLOGY OF SENSES
descriptions: A part of perceptual psychology that deals with the hardware and mechanics of how the body senses the world.
PHYSIOLOGY OF SENSES.description: A part of perceptual psychology that deals with the hardware and mechanics of how the body senses the world.

HUMAN FACTORS IN XR.name: HUMAN FACTORS IN XR
descriptions: The study of how humans interact with and perceive virtual and augmented reality systems, specifically focusing on the process of perception.
HUMAN FACTORS IN XR.description: The study of how humans interact with and perceive virtual and augmented reality systems, specifically focusing on the process of perception.

NEURON.name: NEURON
descriptions: A basic structural and functional unit of the nervous system, characterized by a nucleus or cell body that performs processing on inputs.
The biological units that receive inputs from receptors and aggregate information into higher-level signals.
Cells that receive signals from receptors and transmit messages through a neural network.
NEURON.description: A basic structural and functional unit of the nervous system, characterized by a nucleus or cell body that performs processing on inputs. The biological units that receive inputs from receptors and aggregate information into higher-level signals. Cells that receive signals from receptors and transmit messages through a neural network.

CELL BODY.name: CELL BODY
descriptions: The nucleus or main body of a neuron, which serves as a node in the brain's graph and performs processing on input signals.
CELL BODY.description: The nucleus or main body of a neuron, which serves as a node in the brain's graph and performs processing on input signals.

DENDRITES.name: DENDRITES
descriptions: The input edges of a neuron that allow it to aggregate information from other neurons.
DENDRITES.description: The input edges of a neuron that allow it to aggregate information from other neurons.

AXONS.name: AXONS
descriptions: The output edges of a neuron through which processed signals are transmitted to other neurons.
AXONS.description: The output edges of a neuron through which processed signals are transmitted to other neurons.

NEURAL NETWORK.name: NEURAL NETWORK
descriptions: A model of interconnection of neurons used as the original idea behind machine learning and deep learning approaches.
The system through which neural impulses are transmitted to the brain.
A system meant for transferring neural information from one neuron to another.
NEURAL NETWORK.description: A model of interconnection of neurons used as the original idea behind machine learning and deep learning approaches. A system meant for transferring neural information from one neuron to another. The system through which neural impulses are transmitted to the brain.

SYNAPSE.name: SYNAPSE
descriptions: A gap between the axon of one neuron and the dendrite of the next where electrical or chemical signals are passed.
SYNAPSE.description: A gap between the axon of one neuron and the dendrite of the next where electrical or chemical signals are passed.

HIERARCHICAL PROCESSING.name: HIERARCHICAL PROCESSING
descriptions: A process where signals from sense organ receptors propagate through the neural network to the cerebral cortex, undergoing selective processing along the way.
A type of processing where information is aggregated in stages through neurons to detect increasingly complex patterns in a stimulus.
HIERARCHICAL PROCESSING.description: A process where signals from sense organ receptors propagate through the neural network to the cerebral cortex, undergoing selective processing along the way. A type of processing where information is aggregated in stages through neurons to detect increasingly complex patterns in a stimulus.

SELECTIVITY.name: SELECTIVITY
descriptions: The property where each receptor responds to only a narrow range of stimuli across time, space, and frequency.
SELECTIVITY.description: The property where each receptor responds to only a narrow range of stimuli across time, space, and frequency.

CEREBRAL CORTEX.name: CEREBRAL CORTEX
descriptions: The final destination in the brain where signals from receptors eventually reach after hierarchical processing.
The part of the human brain where sensory signals are combined with long-term memory for the interpretation of stimuli.
A part of the brain that receives signals from the motor cortex along with other brain regions.
CEREBRAL CORTEX.description: The part of the human brain where sensory signals are combined with long-term memory for the interpretation of stimuli. The final destination in the brain where signals from receptors eventually reach after hierarchical processing. A part of the brain that receives signals from the motor cortex along with other brain regions.

DEEP LEARNING.name: DEEP LEARNING
descriptions: A subset of machine learning based on the principles of neural networks.
An omnipresent concept for building better experiences and more intelligent systems.
DEEP LEARNING.description: An omnipresent concept for building better experiences and more intelligent systems. A subset of machine learning based on the principles of neural networks.

RECEPTORS.name: RECEPTORS
descriptions: Sensory structures that respond to specific stimuli and initiate signal propagation through the neural network.
Biological components in human physiology, specifically in the skin, that receive input from the real world to process information for touch perception.
RECEPTORS.description: Biological components in human physiology, specifically in the skin, that receive input from the real world to process information for touch perception. Sensory structures that respond to specific stimuli and initiate signal propagation through the neural network.

STIMULUS.name: STIMULUS
descriptions: The external input or data that is received by receptors and undergoes hierarchical processing and interpretation.
STIMULUS.description: The external input or data that is received by receptors and undergoes hierarchical processing and interpretation.

PERCEPTUAL PHENOMENA.name: PERCEPTUAL PHENOMENA
descriptions: The result of combining sensory inputs with experience, including examples like face recognition and identification of a song.

Outcomes resulting from the combination of hierarchical processing and the combination of real-time sensory input with long-term knowledge or experience, such as face recognition and song identification.
PERCEPTUAL PHENOMENA.description: Outcomes resulting from the combination of hierarchical processing and the combination of real-time sensory input with long-term knowledge or experience, such as face recognition and song identification. The result of combining sensory inputs with experience, including examples like face recognition and identification of a song.

RECEPTOR R1.name: RECEPTOR R1
descriptions: One of the specific receptors (R1, R2, R3, R4) that provide initial inputs for neural aggregation.
RECEPTOR R1.description: One of the specific receptors (R1, R2, R3, R4) that provide initial inputs for neural aggregation.

RECEPTOR R2.name: RECEPTOR R2
descriptions: One of the specific receptors (R1, R2, R3, R4) that provide initial inputs for neural aggregation.
RECEPTOR R2.description: One of the specific receptors (R1, R2, R3, R4) that provide initial inputs for neural aggregation.

NEURON 1.name: NEURON 1
descriptions: A specific neuron that aggregates information from receptors R1 and R2.
NEURON 1.description: A specific neuron that aggregates information from receptors R1 and R2.

NEURON 2.name: NEURON 2
descriptions: A specific neuron that aggregates information from receptors R3 and R4.
NEURON 2.description: A specific neuron that aggregates information from receptors R3 and R4.

NEURON N3.name: NEURON N3
descriptions: A neuron that receives aggregated information from Neuron 1 and Neuron 2 to create even higher-level information.
NEURON N3.description: A neuron that receives aggregated information from Neuron 1 and Neuron 2 to create even higher-level information.

FACE RECOGNITION.name: FACE RECOGNITION
descriptions: A specific perceptual phenomenon mentioned as an outcome of combined knowledge and sensory input.
FACE RECOGNITION.description: A specific perceptual phenomenon mentioned as an outcome of combined knowledge and sensory input.

IDENTIFICATION OF A SONG.name: IDENTIFICATION OF A SONG
descriptions: A specific perceptual phenomenon resulting from knowledge of music and interpretation of sound waves.
IDENTIFICATION OF A SONG.description: A specific perceptual phenomenon resulting from knowledge of music and interpretation of sound waves.

MUSIC.name: MUSIC
descriptions: An experience characterized by rhythm; requires prior knowledge to interpret corresponding sound waves.
MUSIC.description: An experience characterized by rhythm; requires prior knowledge to interpret corresponding sound waves.

FACE.name: FACE
descriptions: An entity that requires prior knowledge (human or animal) to be identified from light patterns received by the eyes.
FACE.description: An entity that requires prior knowledge (human or animal) to be identified from light patterns received by the eyes.

SENSORY ORGANS.name: SENSORY ORGANS
descriptions: Physical organs that receive raw stimuli from the environment, including vision, auditory sense, touch, smell, and taste.
SENSORY ORGANS.description: Physical organs that receive raw stimuli from the environment, including vision, auditory sense, touch, smell, and taste.

PROPRIOCEPTION.name: PROPRIOCEPTION
descriptions: The ability to sense the relative positions of body parts and the amount of muscular effort involved in moving them, often referred to as the "sixth sense.
The sense of self-movement and body position, which may conflict with visual input in a virtual environment.
A sense that provides information which can conflict with vision, potentially causing sensory conflict.
The sixth sense, defined as the awareness of the pose of each movable human body part.
The sense of the relative position of body parts and the movement of those parts, involving receptors like muscle spindles and Golgi tendon organs.
A sense of self-movement and body position, related to the human somatosensory system and kinesthesis.
PROPRIOCEPTION.description: The ability to sense the relative positions of body parts and the amount of muscular effort involved in moving them, often referred to as the "sixth sense. The sense of the relative position of body parts and the movement of those parts, involving receptors like muscle spindles and Golgi tendon organs. The sense of self-movement and body position, which may conflict with visual input in a virtual environment. A sense that provides information which can conflict with vision, potentially causing sensory conflict.

MOTOR CORTEX.name: MOTOR CORTEX
descriptions: A part of the brain that controls body motion and sends signals called efference copies to other parts of the brain.
MOTOR CORTEX.description: A part of the brain that controls body motion and sends signals called efference copies to other parts of the brain.

EFFERENCE COPIES.name: EFFERENCE COPIES
descriptions: Signals sent by the motor cortex to other parts of the brain to communicate executed motions.
EFFERENCE COPIES.description: Signals sent by the motor cortex to other parts of the brain to communicate executed motions.

SIXTH SENSE.name: SIXTH SENSE
descriptions: A term used to describe proprioception, as it lacks a dedicated sensory organ or receptor.
SIXTH SENSE.description: A term used to describe proprioception, as it lacks a dedicated sensory organ or receptor.

LEARNING.name: LEARNING
descriptions: The process of obtaining experience over a long period of time, allowing the brain to interpret inputs in coherent and familiar ways.
LEARNING.description: The process of obtaining experience over a long period of time, allowing the brain to interpret inputs in coherent and familiar ways.

BRAIN DEVELOPMENT.name: BRAIN DEVELOPMENT
descriptions: The process of learning perception and cognition over a long period of time.
BRAIN DEVELOPMENT.description: The process of learning perception and cognition over a long period of time.

MISMATCH.name: MISMATCH
descriptions: The conflict between data from senses and the brain's learned processing methods, often occurring when experiencing a VR system.
MISMATCH.description: The conflict between data from senses and the brain's learned processing methods, often occurring when experiencing a VR system.

SENSORY CONFLICT.name: SENSORY CONFLICT
descriptions: A mismatch where vision tells one thing while the balance sense and proprioception tell something else, which can lead to cybersickness or compromised presence.
SENSORY CONFLICT.description: A mismatch where vision tells one thing while the balance sense and proprioception tell something else, which can lead to cybersickness or compromised presence.

HUMAN PHYSIOLOGY.name: HUMAN PHYSIOLOGY
descriptions: The study of the human body's functions, which provides an overview for designing VR systems.
The biological functions and physical structures of the human body and how they relate to the usage of AR-VR systems.
HUMAN PHYSIOLOGY.description: The biological functions and physical structures of the human body and how they relate to the usage of AR-VR systems. The study of the human body's functions, which provides an overview for designing VR systems.

PROCESS OF PERCEPTION.name: PROCESS OF PERCEPTION
descriptions: The way humans perceive information, studied in the context of designing VR systems.
PROCESS OF PERCEPTION.description: The way humans perceive information, studied in the context of designing VR systems.

HUMAN PSYCHOLOGY.name: HUMAN PSYCHOLOGY
descriptions: The study of human minds and behaviors, which provides basics for XR design.
HUMAN PSYCHOLOGY.description: The study of human minds and behaviors, which provides basics for XR design.

AR/VR SYSTEMS.name: AR/VR SYSTEMS
descriptions: Systems related to Augmented Reality and Virtual Reality that are dictated by human physiology for design purposes.
AR/VR SYSTEMS.description: Systems related to Augmented Reality and Virtual Reality that are dictated by human physiology for design purposes.

LENSES.name: LENSES
descriptions: Optical components that guide light to the eyes; can be engineered (part of a headset) or natural (parts of the eyes).
Parts of the eye and parts of a headset that, when combined, help users perceive immersive visual content by propagating light.
Physical components whose operation is explained using the concept of light as a ray.
LENSES.description: Parts of the eye and parts of a headset that, when combined, help users perceive immersive visual content by propagating light. Optical components that guide light to the eyes; can be engineered (part of a headset) or natural (parts of the eyes). Physical components whose operation is explained using the concept of light as a ray.

ENGINEERED LENSES.name: ENGINEERED LENSES
descriptions: Man-made lenses that are part of the headset hardware used to guide light.
ENGINEERED LENSES.description: Man-made lenses that are part of the headset hardware used to guide light.

NATURAL LENSES.name: NATURAL LENSES
descriptions: Biological lenses that are part of the human eye's anatomy.
NATURAL LENSES.description: Biological lenses that are part of the human eye's anatomy.

RETINAS.name: RETINAS
descriptions: Parts of the human eye where light from displays arrives to facilitate visual perception.
RETINAS.description: Parts of the human eye where light from displays arrives to facilitate visual perception.

VISUAL PERCEPTION.name: VISUAL PERCEPTION
descriptions: The process of interpreting light to perceive immersive visual content, resulting from the interaction of light, lenses, and the eye.
The process by which the human eye and brain interpret light propagation and lens interaction to perceive a scene or immersive visual content.
One of the senses used to perceive information, which alone may not provide a complete picture of a virtual experience.
VISUAL PERCEPTION.description: The process by which the human eye and brain interpret light propagation and lens interaction to perceive a scene or immersive visual content. The process of interpreting light to perceive immersive visual content, resulting from the interaction of light, lenses, and the eye. One of the senses used to perceive information, which alone may not provide a complete picture of a virtual experience.

VIRTUAL WORLDS.name: VIRTUAL WORLDS
descriptions: Digital environments that can be modeled using the physics of light propagation and camera configurations to create immersive experiences.
VIRTUAL WORLDS.description: Digital environments that can be modeled using the physics of light propagation and camera configurations to create immersive experiences.

TRACKING HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE.name: TRACKING HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE
descriptions: Systems built to track movement or position, which are improved by understanding visual senses and camera mechanics.
TRACKING HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE.description: Systems built to track movement or position, which are improved by understanding visual senses and camera mechanics.

PHOTONS.name: PHOTONS
descriptions: Tiny particles of energy that move through space at high speeds (speed of light); used to calculate the amount of light received by sensors or receptors.
A particle view of light; a hypothetical particle whose traces of motion can be used to describe light as rays and calculate the amount of light received at sensors.
PHOTONS.description: A particle view of light; a hypothetical particle whose traces of motion can be used to describe light as rays and calculate the amount of light received at sensors. Tiny particles of energy that move through space at high speeds (speed of light); used to calculate the amount of light received by sensors or receptors.

SPEED OF LIGHT.name: SPEED OF LIGHT
descriptions: The high speed at which photons/energy particles move through space.
SPEED OF LIGHT.description: The high speed at which photons/energy particles move through space.

SENSOR OR RECEPTOR.name: SENSOR OR RECEPTOR
descriptions: Components that receive light; understanding photons helps in calculating the amount of light received by these components.
SENSOR OR RECEPTOR.description: Components that receive light; understanding photons helps in calculating the amount of light received by these components.

WAVES.name: WAVES
descriptions: A description of light as ripples through space, which is helpful in understanding the spectrum of color.
WAVES.description: A description of light as ripples through space, which is helpful in understanding the spectrum of color.

RAYS.name: RAYS
descriptions: A description of light as traces of motion of a single hypothetical photon or a trajectory; helpful in explaining how lenses work and the concept of visibility.
RAYS.description: A description of light as traces of motion of a single hypothetical photon or a trajectory; helpful in explaining how lenses work and the concept of visibility.

COLOR.name: COLOR
descriptions: A phenomenon explained in terms of light as a wave rather than a particle.
The attributes assigned to objects and interface components to define their appearance.
An attribute assigned to objects that enables the perception of depth and realism in a 3D scene; if not assigned properly, it reduces the quality of experience.
COLOR.description: An attribute assigned to objects that enables the perception of depth and realism in a 3D scene; if not assigned properly, it reduces the quality of experience. The attributes assigned to objects and interface components to define their appearance. A phenomenon explained in terms of light as a wave rather than a particle.

INTERACTION WITH MATERIAL.name: INTERACTION WITH MATERIAL
descriptions: The interaction that occurs between light and a material when light falls on it, involving transmission, absorption, or reflection.
INTERACTION WITH MATERIAL.description: The interaction that occurs between light and a material when light falls on it, involving transmission, absorption, or reflection.

TRANSMISSION.name: TRANSMISSION
descriptions: A phenomenon where some part of the light rays passes through a material and goes out of the other side.
The process where light rays pass through a surface.
The process of light falling, passing through, and emerging from a surface.
TRANSMISSION.description: A phenomenon where some part of the light rays passes through a material and goes out of the other side. The process of light falling, passing through, and emerging from a surface. The process where light rays pass through a surface.

ABSORPTION.name: ABSORPTION
descriptions: A phenomenon where some part of the light rays terminate within the material or object with no further propagation outside.
The process where light rays are taken in by a surface rather than being reflected or transmitted.
ABSORPTION.description: A phenomenon where some part of the light rays terminate within the material or object with no further propagation outside. The process where light rays are taken in by a surface rather than being reflected or transmitted.

REFLECTION.name: REFLECTION
descriptions: A phenomenon where the ray falls on the surface and gets reflected from the surface without entering or penetrating the object.
The process where light rays strike a surface and bounce back without entering or penetrating the object.
The final step performed after the final drawing of ideas
The process of analyzing and reflecting on data collected during inquiry to generate design recommendations and understand user needs.
The process where emitted light falls on a surface and bounces off, either toward the viewer's eye or onto other surfaces.
REFLECTION.description: The process of analyzing and reflecting on data collected during inquiry to generate design recommendations and understand user needs. A phenomenon where the ray falls on the surface and gets reflected from the surface without entering or penetrating the object. The process where emitted light falls on a surface and bounces off, either toward the viewer's eye or onto other surfaces. The process where light rays strike a surface and bounce back without entering or penetrating the object.

VISIBILITY.name: VISIBILITY
descriptions: A concept whose explanation is aided by the idea of light as a ray.
VISIBILITY.description: A concept whose explanation is aided by the idea of light as a ray.

LIGHT RAYS.name: LIGHT RAYS
descriptions: Electromagnetic waves that interact with surfaces through reflection, absorption, or transmission. They are the primary medium for transmitting visual information.
The rays that are reflected from surfaces and enter the eye to be refracted and focused.
Parallel rays of light entering from the left side that fall on the eye or lens system.
LIGHT RAYS.description: Electromagnetic waves that interact with surfaces through reflection, absorption, or transmission. They are the primary medium for transmitting visual information. The rays that are reflected from surfaces and enter the eye to be refracted and focused. Parallel rays of light entering from the left side that fall on the eye or lens system.

COLOR PERCEPTION.name: COLOR PERCEPTION
descriptions: The process by which the human eye perceives the color of a point or scene, determined by the intensity of reflected light rays reaching the viewer's eye.
The ability to perceive colors, which is accomplished through photopic vision using cones.
The process by which humans perceive colors as a combination of different amounts of red, green, and blue light.
The result of the intensity of reflected light reaching the viewer's eye, determining what color the viewer perceives.
COLOR PERCEPTION.description: The process by which the human eye perceives the color of a point or scene, determined by the intensity of reflected light rays reaching the viewer's eye. The result of the intensity of reflected light reaching the viewer's eye, determining what color the viewer perceives. The process by which humans perceive colors as a combination of different amounts of red, green, and blue light. The ability to perceive colors, which is accomplished through photopic vision using cones.

INCIDENT LIGHT.name: INCIDENT LIGHT
descriptions: Light that falls onto a surface from a source.
INCIDENT LIGHT.description: Light that falls onto a surface from a source.

SOURCE OF LIGHT.name: SOURCE OF LIGHT
descriptions: The origin of light rays that interact with surfaces to eventually reach the viewer's eye.
SOURCE OF LIGHT.description: The origin of light rays that interact with surfaces to eventually reach the viewer's eye.

INTENSITY OF THE RAY.name: INTENSITY OF THE RAY
descriptions: The measure of the amount of light that reaches the viewer's eye, which determines the perceived color.
INTENSITY OF THE RAY.description: The measure of the amount of light that reaches the viewer's eye, which determines the perceived color.

VIEWER'S EYE.name: VIEWER'S EYE
descriptions: The organ of the human visual perceptual system that receives reflected light to facilitate color perception.
VIEWER'S EYE.description: The organ of the human visual perceptual system that receives reflected light to facilitate color perception.

SURROUNDING OBJECTS.name: SURROUNDING OBJECTS
descriptions: Objects in the environment that can reflect light indirectly toward the viewer.
SURROUNDING OBJECTS.description: Objects in the environment that can reflect light indirectly toward the viewer.

AMBIENT LIGHT.name: AMBIENT LIGHT
descriptions: Light in the environment that is reflected from surrounding objects and mixes with light from direct sources to reach the eye.
Light that falls on the surface of an object after being reflected from surrounding surfaces; represented by the intensity I_amb.
AMBIENT LIGHT.description: Light that falls on the surface of an object after being reflected from surrounding surfaces; represented by the intensity I_amb. Light in the environment that is reflected from surrounding objects and mixes with light from direct sources to reach the eye.

VISUAL PERCEPTUAL SYSTEM.name: VISUAL PERCEPTUAL SYSTEM
descriptions: The human biological system responsible for processing visual information, which must be understood to design good systems or identify flaws.
VISUAL PERCEPTUAL SYSTEM.description: The human biological system responsible for processing visual information, which must be understood to design good systems or identify flaws.

CORNEA.name: CORNEA
descriptions: The outer surface of the eye through which light rays pass and are refracted to focus images on the retina.
A component of the human eye considered to be a powerful lens with a fixed focal depth.
The first of two convex lenses in the human eye, acting as a lens with an optical power of approximately 40 diopters.
A physical part of the human eye that works in combination with the lens to focus images of faraway objects onto the retina.
CORNEA.description: A physical part of the human eye that works in combination with the lens to focus images of faraway objects onto the retina. The first of two convex lenses in the human eye, acting as a lens with an optical power of approximately 40 diopters. The outer surface of the eye through which light rays pass and are refracted to focus images on the retina. A component of the human eye considered to be a powerful lens with a fixed focal depth.

PUPIL.name: PUPIL
descriptions: An opening in the eye whose size can be changed (dilated or constricted) to control the amount of light entering the eye.
PUPIL.description: An opening in the eye whose size can be changed (dilated or constricted) to control the amount of light entering the eye.

LENS.name: LENS
descriptions: A component of the eye that, along with the cornea, refracts light rays to focus images on the retina.
A physical part of the eye that, along with the cornea, provides optical power to focus light onto the retina.
LENS.description: A physical part of the eye that, along with the cornea, provides optical power to focus light onto the retina. A component of the eye that, along with the cornea, refracts light rays to focus images on the retina.

RETINA.name: RETINA
descriptions: A component located at the back side of the eye that contains photoreceptors and optic nerve fibers; it receives focused images.
The part of the eye containing photoreceptors (rods and cones).
The part of the eye where photoreceptors (rods and cones) are located, where density variations lead to different types of vision.
The part of the eye where light is received, described as being "inside out" and containing photoreceptors.
The image surface or portion of the eye where light rays fall and are transmitted to the brain via optical nerves; it is a non-planar, spherically curved surface.
A non-planar, spherically curved surface within the human eye that contains photoreceptors to convert light into neural pulses; it replaces the concept of a focal plane.
The part of the eye where images are focused and where real images must be formed for human perception to occur.
RETINA.description: A non-planar, spherically curved surface within the human eye that contains photoreceptors to convert light into neural pulses; it replaces the concept of a focal plane. The image surface or portion of the eye where light rays fall and are transmitted to the brain via optical nerves; it is a non-planar, spherically curved surface. The part of the eye where photoreceptors (rods and cones) are located, where density variations lead to different types of vision. A component located at the back side of the eye that contains photoreceptors and optic nerve fibers; it receives focused images.

IRIS.name: IRIS
descriptions: The part of the eye that determines the change in pupil size, controlling the amount of light entering the eye based on brightness.
IRIS.description: The part of the eye that determines the change in pupil size, controlling the amount of light entering the eye based on brightness.

REFRACTION.name: REFRACTION
descriptions: The process by which the material of the cornea and lens bends light rays to focus images on the retina.
REFRACTION.description: The process by which the material of the cornea and lens bends light rays to focus images on the retina.

VISION PHYSIOLOGY.name: VISION PHYSIOLOGY
descriptions: The study and understanding of how the human vision system and bodily sensors work.
VISION PHYSIOLOGY.description: The study and understanding of how the human vision system and bodily sensors work.

OPTIC NERVE FIBERS.name: OPTIC NERVE FIBERS
descriptions: Neurons located in the retina that take the signal from the eye to the brain.
OPTIC NERVE FIBERS.description: Neurons located in the retina that take the signal from the eye to the brain.

RODS.name: RODS
descriptions: One of the two types of photoreceptors in the human eye, more numerous in the peripheral region of the retina.
A type of photoreceptor that is more numerous in the peripheral region of the retina; multiple rods can share one optic nerve, which aids in sensitivity to lower levels of light.
Photoreceptors in the retina that are more prevalent in the peripheral region and help with movement detection.
RODS.description: A type of photoreceptor that is more numerous in the peripheral region of the retina; multiple rods can share one optic nerve, which aids in sensitivity to lower levels of light. Photoreceptors in the retina that are more prevalent in the peripheral region and help with movement detection. One of the two types of photoreceptors in the human eye, more numerous in the peripheral region of the retina.

CONES.name: CONES
descriptions: One of the two types of photoreceptors in the human eye, mainly located in a small central region called the fovea.
A type of photoreceptor mainly located in a small central region of the retina called the fovea; there is more or less one optic nerve fiber for each cone, which aids in image resolution and acuity.
